issues.note: Split-support citation. Official-Guide p.3 supports the response-format half verbatim ('All questions on the exam are multiple choice format. Each question has one correct response and three incorrect responses.' / 'Select the single response that best completes the statement or answers the question.'). It does NOT support 'no partial credit within a question' -- the words 'partial credit' appear nowhere in the official guide. That clause comes only from Exam-Mechanics_v2 Scoring Context ('No partial credit; platform forces an answer on every question') and Domain weights ('No partial credit per question.'). Since the guide is the leading cite, a reader checking p.3 for the partial-credit rule finds nothing. Cleanest fix: drop the partial-credit half from front and back, leaving a fully guide-backed format card. If the deck wants the partial-credit point kept, it must be its own card citing Exam-Mechanics_v2 Scoring Context alone. Note the claim is a tautology of single-answer MC, not an independent exam rule -- the guide's silence is expected, not an omission.

issues.note: The front asks three things and the back answers two. 'Leave a question blank' is answered by the guide (p.3: 'The exam platform requires an answer to every question before you can advance, so no question is left unanswered.'). 'Come back to it' is not: neither the official guide nor Exam-Mechanics_v2 says anything about back-navigation or whether a submitted answer can be revised. Drilling this front risks the learner concluding answers lock, which no source states. Separately, on provenance: the 'a wrong answer carries no penalty' half is NOT in the official guide -- the guide never mentions penalties or negative marking. It rests entirely on Exam-Mechanics_v2 (Format: 'no skip, no penalty for wrong answers'; Scoring Context: 'guessing costs nothing'), which itself gives no external source. The card's cite ORDER already handles this correctly (Exam-Mechanics_v2 primary, Official-Guide p.3 second), so no cite change is needed -- this note records the finding.

issues.note: 'About 15 per block' is project arithmetic, not a published figure. The official guide never states a per-scenario question count. Its only per-scenario language is p.4: 'Each scenario presents a realistic production context that frames a set of questions' -- set sizes unspecified, and no statement that the split is even. The number is derived in Exam-Mechanics_v2 Scenario Bank, which is explicit that it is a division: '(~15 per scenario at 60 questions / 4 scenarios)'. Typed as 'fact' with a bare 'About 15', the card presents a division as a published number; a real sitting could block 20/15/15/10 without contradicting anything Anthropic wrote. Keep the number (it is the right pacing heuristic) but make the derivation visible.

issues.note: LOWEST SEVERITY -- content and cite are exact ('Validity period 12 months from the date the credential is awarded', Official-Guide p.2), and the card does read sensibly reversed. The issue is quota: CARD-SPEC 9 targets under 10% of facts carrying rev, and the deck sits at 13.6% (9 rev on 66 facts) with 4 of those 9 in this 14-card file -- every other deck file carries exactly 1. This is the lowest-yield of the four (core: false, non-scored logistics), so it is the one to spend out of the rapid-fire Numbers drill. Dropping it takes the deck to 12.1%. Optional; triage last.

The only card in the file whose factual content cannot be checked against any document in this project. The official guide says nothing about retakes -- no attempt limit, no waiting period, no retake section at all. The claim traces to Exam-Mechanics_v2 Format: 'Retakes | Max 4 attempts per rolling 12 months; waiting periods apply between attempts (per Pearson VUE policy pages, retrieved 2026-07-06)'. Those policy pages are not in the repo, so this is third-hand and unverifiable here. Credit where due: the card cites Exam-Mechanics_v2 only, adds no Official-Guide cite, and says so in the back -- the provenance handling is the most honest in the file. Two remaining defects: 'with waiting periods between attempts' names no duration, so it is not a retrievable fact; and the whole card is non-scored logistics with zero exam-mark value. Killing it outright costs nothing and is equally defensible.

Applied by the same edit. CARD-SPEC 2 allows a second sentence in the back only when it adds a distinct fact; 'This limit comes from the test-delivery policy pages, not the official Exam Guide' is sourcing metadata, not a fact about the exam, and it restates what the sole Exam-Mechanics_v2 cite already signals. If the deck owner prefers the warning to survive into the drilled text rather than live in the cite, keep a short clause -- but then it should be the only second sentence, with the unquantified waiting-period phrase still dropped.

D5's 15% is NOT -- the Content Outline breaks mid-list and 'Domain 5: Context Management & Reliability (15% of scored content)' is the first line of p.4 (line 79). Separately, this claim is 100% official-guide material, yet the derived summary leads the cite list; CARD-SPEC 6 requires the primary cite to be the section the claim is drawn from. Fix both at once by citing the two guide pages, exactly as ex-008 already does for the six scenarios that span pp.4-5.
